operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are mixed-case (Party_ID, Is_Main_in_Charge); must double-quote with original spelling.
DDL uses backtick-quoted FK parents (`host`, `party`) — sqlite_master text must be replayed verbatim; backticks are valid sqlite quoting.
First_year/Last_year/Age are declared TEXT but store 4-digit years / ages as text; TS dispatches them to String, not Date/Number.
Is_Main_in_Charge declared bool, storage class text with values 'T'/'F' (not 1/0) — Bool fuzzer emits True/False/1/0, contradicting storage.
party_host is a pure junction: composite PK (Party_ID,Host_ID), both columns also FKs to party/host; PK members are FK children.
All columns notnull=0, so TS may insert NULLs into PK/FK columns; sqlite PK on non-INTEGER columns allows NULLs, so PK dedup may not catch NULL rows.
Tiny tables (8/10/6 rows) — choose_table_sizes will massively over-generate vs original; FK child draws from small parent pools with replacement.
party_host.Party_ID distinct=5 < party rows=8 and Host_ID distinct=6 < host rows=10 — original junction is sparse, not a full cross product.
No unique/check constraints, no indexes, no views/triggers in DDL.
Location has trailing-space and comma-joined multi-value samples ('Hemkade 48 Zaandam, Heineken Music Hall ') — string contamination will look plausible.
Number_of_hosts values (5,23,4,6,31) exceed party_host row counts — no FK-like consistency between it and junction rows.
operator_ts_expectations: Party_ID/Host_ID/Number_of_hosts -> Number fuzzer, scale 0, range [-1,1] full-range draws plus +-1/+-2 perturbations of sampled elements; fresh draws cluster near 0, far from original 1..10.
Party_Theme/Location/Name/Nationality -> String fuzzer, length range from samples, CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() with 50% contamination — produces implausible names/locations.
First_year/Last_year/Age -> String fuzzer (declared TEXT), so years become random strings, not 4-digit years; int-like elements get +-1 variants only.
Is_Main_in_Charge -> Bool fuzzer emits True/False (Python bools -> 1/0 in sqlite), contradicting original 'T'/'F' text storage.
party_host FK columns draw from party.Party_ID / host.Host_ID final filtered values with replacement; PK dedup then drops duplicate (Party_ID,Host_ID) pairs, shrinking junction below requested size.
Because PK members are also FK children, sample_fresh_primary_keys runs after FK fill; composite-PK member max_l0=30 caps fresh draws, so junction values are mostly reused parent keys.
Expected FN: gold queries filtering on 'T'/'F', on year strings like '2000', or on specific themes/locations will get no matching rows from contaminated strings.
Expected FP: gold queries with COUNT/aggregate or DISTINCT over tiny tables may coincidentally match because TS over-generates rows and aggregates saturate.
Expected FP: queries relying on junction sparsity (e.g. hosts per party) may match by luck since TS junction is near-dense over small parent pools.
Expected FN: queries on Number_of_hosts vs actual junction counts — TS never ties the two, so consistency queries fail both ways.
Expected FP: empty-result gold queries (e.g. impossible year) may return rows because String fuzzer emits arbitrary text that occasionally matches.
No Date/Time fuzzers fire here; no crash-fallback types; no dangling FKs; no self-references.
